newsitem.title: GERMANY: German shares close bourse down, consolidating.
newsitem.headline: German shares close bourse down, consolidating.

text.p: German shares ended bourse dealings slightly lower on Monday, weighed down by a weaker dollar, with dealers saying the market was consolidating following record-breaking run of recent weeks.

The DAX index of 30 leading shares closed floor trade down 5.79 points, or 0.21 percent, at 2,729.03 and was unable to hold advances made in electronic trade, which was boosted after data showed some slowing in German money supply growth.

The IBIS DAX, which reflects all-day computer dealings in the DAX, had jumped to a new record of 2,745.82 points after the German central bank said money supply growth in September was an annualised 8.4 percent compared to 8.7 in August.

Dealers said some players were taking profit and the market was in a consolidation phase after new record high levels were reached last week. "The market could fall a little bit further in the short term," said one.
Preferred shares in software manufacturer SAP AG lost nearly two percent, to end floor trade down 4.70 marks at 279.30 marks. Traders said they saw some profit-taking on the stock.

German plant manufacturing group Duerr AG lost ten percent to end bourse dealings down 5.50 marks at 49.50 marks after the firm said it expected 1996 profits to be lower than the 43.9 million earned in the previous year.

National telecommunications monopoly Deutsche Telekom announced a price range of between 25 and 30 marks, in line with most forecasts, for the some 500 million shares in its initial public offering next month.
Dealers said Telekom shares were fetching between 37 and 39 marks in unofficial or so-called "grey trade".
